issues.legal_issue: A transfer made in breach of an interim injunction remains subject to the consequences of that breach when the injunction was operative at the time of transfer, even if the plaint is later returned for presentation to a competent court.
material_facts: An interim injunction restrained alienation of the suit property.
The property was transferred while the injunction remained operative.
The plaint was returned for presentation to a competent court only after the transfer.
issues.conclusion: The injunction remained effective when the transfer was made, and the transfer appeared unlawful; the eventual return of the plaint did not erase the consequences of a violation committed while the injunction was in force.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, an agreement whose object or consideration is forbidden by law, defeats a legal provision, or involves injury to another's property is unlawful. Tayabbhai M. Bagasarwalla v. Hind Rubber Industries Pvt. Ltd. (1997) 3 SCC 443 holds that interim orders are effective while in force and must be obeyed, and that a breach committed before a decision on jurisdiction can still have consequences after that decision. Vidur Impex and Traders (P) Ltd. v. Tosh Apartments (P) Ltd. (2012) 8 SCC 384 holds that transactions made in clear violation of an injunction restraining alienation lack legal sanctity.

predicates.civil_suit_with_interim_injunction: A civil suit was brought in which the court issued an interim injunction.
predicates.transfer_of_restrained_property: A party transferred property that the injunction restrained that party from alienating.
predicates.injunction_operational_at_transfer: The injunction remained in force when the transfer occurred.
predicates.transfer_appears_unlawful: The transfer appears unlawful because it was made in breach of the operative injunction.

issues.definition: When a party transfers restrained property while an interim injunction in a civil suit is in force, the transfer appears unlawful.

issues.legal_issue: A second appeal cannot be summarily dismissed as raising no substantial question of law when it challenges the legality of a transfer made during the operation of an injunction restraining that transfer.
material_facts: The transfer challenged in the second appeal occurred while an injunction restraining alienation was operative.
The second appeal raised the legal effect of that transfer.
The High Court summarily dismissed the second appeal on the ground that no substantial question of law arose.
issues.conclusion: The legality of the transfer raised a substantial question of law under Section 100(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the summary dismissal was erroneous; the second appeal had to be heard afresh.
issues.legal_principle: Section 100(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure permits a second appeal where a substantial question of law arises. The proposition in Amar Chand Inani v. Union of India (1973) 1 SCC 115, that a suit is deemed filed when its plaint is presented to the competent court, did not answer the separate question of the legality of a transfer made while an injunction was operative. Tayabbhai M. Bagasarwalla v. Hind Rubber Industries Pvt. Ltd. (1997) 3 SCC 443 and Vidur Impex and Traders (P) Ltd. v. Tosh Apartments (P) Ltd. (2012) 8 SCC 384 support the legal significance of a transfer made in breach of an operative injunction.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is a second appeal.
predicates.transfer_challenged_as_breach_of_injunct: The appeal challenges the legality of a transfer on the ground that it breached an injunction.
predicates.injunction_operational_at_transfer: The injunction remained in force when the transfer occurred.
predicates.summary_dismissal_for_no_substantial_que: The second appeal was summarily dismissed on the basis that no substantial question of law arose.
predicates.second_appeal_requires_fresh_hearing: The second appeal must be heard afresh with the substantial question of law considered.

issues.definition: A second appeal challenging a transfer made in breach of an operative injunction requires a fresh hearing when it was summarily dismissed as raising no substantial question of law.
